situation:
You are the promotion director for IRONBRIDGE ROLLER DERBY LEAGUE, a profitable company that runs a twenty-team roller derby season and a youth community sports program out of a single arena. The founder (judge) started the league twelve years ago, has run it in the black for nine of them, and is preparing to hand the business to new ownership at the end of this season.

The league has never sold broadcast rights. Every bout streams free on the league's own site, and each viewer who signs in leaves an email address and a mobile number. That list reaches nine thousand fans directly, and it is what the league's sponsors and the county visitors bureau pay for when they promote bout weekends to travelers who fill the hotels downtown.

STREAMCOURT, a national sports streaming service, has offered a two-year exclusive rights agreement with a guaranteed fee paid in advance. Taking it ends the free stream, moves every bout behind the service's paywall, and turns the viewer contact list over to STREAMCOURT, so the league would give up the direct channel to its nine thousand fans that its sponsors pay for.

The alternative is to spend the cash reserve the founder built over twelve years on the league's own broadcast operation — arena cameras, a production booth, and a subscription app promoted through the league's own email and text messages. It out-earns the STREAMCOURT fee only if the forecast of four thousand paying subscribers holds, and below that number the season closes with the reserve spent and nothing to show for it.

The founder (judge) wants a recommendation on which promotional path to take before the ownership transfer is signed, and wants to hear which one leaves the league's competitive advantage intact for the owner who comes next. The founder (judge) will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the founder (judge) of IRONBRIDGE ROLLER DERBY LEAGUE. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You built the league twelve years ago out of one rented arena night, and you are handing it to new ownership at the end of this season. You want to hear which promotional path the promotion director recommends — the STREAMCOURT agreement or the league's own broadcast operation — and you want to hear how that recommendation would actually be carried out, step by step.

During the presentation you will ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: What is the first step in putting your recommendation in place?
Who does the work of running it once the season starts?
